prerequisites.title: Signed Greenhouse partnership agreement
prerequisites.detail: Required before the OAuth setup steps can proceed. Applications go through Greenhouse's monthly partner review.

prerequisites.title: Publicly reachable callback endpoint
prerequisites.detail: You need a working, tested redirect URI to give Greenhouse. The Composio dashboard shows the redirect URI to copy.

prerequisites.title: 128x128 logo
prerequisites.detail: Customers see it when they authorize your integration.

prerequisites.title: Customer on a supported subscription tier
prerequisites.detail: Harvest v3 partner integrations are listed for Core, Plus and Pro tiers.

steps.title: Submit the integration request form
steps.detail: Fill out Greenhouse's integration request form to start the partner process.

steps.title: Wait for monthly partner review
steps.detail: Requests are reviewed on the first Monday of each month, with a reply within 7 business days after. Off-cycle review is generally only for urgent mutual-customer requests.
steps.done_when: Greenhouse Partnerships contacts you with a decision.

steps.title: Sign the partnership agreement
steps.detail: Legal sign-off is yours; setup steps can only proceed once the agreement is finalized.

steps.title: Draft the credentials request
steps.detail: Prepare integration name, environment (testing or production), required scopes, redirect URI(s) and logo for Partner Support.
steps.done_when: Request email is ready to send.

steps.title: Send request to Partner Support
steps.detail: Email partner-support@greenhouse.io. Greenhouse issues a Client ID and Client Secret.
steps.done_when: Client ID and Client Secret received.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create a custom auth config with your Greenhouse client ID and secret via Composio's API. Keep the secret confidential.
steps.done_when: Auth config exists and a test connection completes.

steps.title: Tell Greenhouse the final redirect URI
steps.detail: Once the callback works and is tested, inform Greenhouse support of the final redirect_uri.
steps.done_when: Greenhouse confirms the redirect URI is registered.

steps.title: Prototype with Composio managed auth
steps.detail: Use the managed greenhouse toolkit to test your agent before your own credentials arrive.

traps.title: Refresh token dies after 14 days unused
traps.detail: Access tokens last 1 hour and refresh tokens 14 days. If a refresh token goes unused for 14 days, the user must redo the full authorization.

traps.title: You cannot change scopes yourself
traps.detail: Scope changes go through Partner Support by email. Requesting scopes not permitted for your client gives an invalid_scope error.

traps.title: Redirect URI must match exactly
traps.detail: A redirect_uri not registered for your client_id returns an invalid_request error.

traps.title: Authorization code lasts 1 minute
traps.detail: Exchange the code immediately with a server-to-server request.

traps.title: Testing credentials are sandbox-only
traps.detail: Testing credentials only work with your own sandbox; production is live for mutual customers.

blockers.what_it_means: The authorizing user lacks the in-app Greenhouse permissions for the action.
blockers.what_to_do: Have a user with the needed permissions authorize, or a Site Admin use a service account.
blockers.agent_can_help: Detect 403 responses and prompt the customer to reconnect with a suitably permissioned user.

blockers.what_it_means: Greenhouse must accept your company first and can decline; the docs describe no self-serve route.
blockers.what_to_do: Contact partneronboarding@greenhouse.io; stay on the managed app meanwhile.

open_questions: Acceptance criteria for partner applications are not documented; ask Greenhouse Partnerships via the integration request form.

The quote says the partner determines whether a Site Admin or standard user should complete setup.
The quote says the option is available only if the authorizing user is a Site Admin.
The quote gives the org-level service user, no username or password, and persistence until disconnected by a permissioned user.

The quote states the authorization code lasts 1 minute and must be exchanged quickly.
The quote says the user may lack the in-app permissions needed for an action, but does not itself tie this to HTTP 403 errors.
The quote says HTTP 403 Forbidden typically relates to permissions.

The quotes say a signed agreement is needed to get started, before the listed steps. The statement places the agreement third, after the form and monthly review.
The quotes give the monthly review cadence and a 7-business-day reply window, which together match the roughly one-month-plus-7-days wait.
